subhead: I turn Google searches into trial bookings for studios, gyms, trainers and coaches.
intro: Fitness is a trial-driven business: someone searches at 10pm, compares three options in four minutes, and books a trial. I do SEO for fitness businesses that wins that window, for pilates studios, personal trainers, boxing gyms and yoga studios.

faqs.q: How long before SEO brings trial bookings to my gym or studio?
faqs.a: Usually three to six months for steady traction. The Google Business Profile work can move the map pack faster, sometimes within weeks, while class and goal pages compound over time. Fitness searches are local and specific, so focused pages tend to move quicker than in broader industries.

faqs.q: I already post on Instagram every day. Isn't that enough?
faqs.a: Instagram keeps current members engaged but rarely brings strangers through the door. Search captures people at the exact moment they decide to start. The fastest-growing fitness businesses use both: social for community, SEO for acquisition.

faqs.q: Should every class type have its own page?
faqs.a: Yes, for every class or goal worth real revenue. People search for the specific thing: reformer, beginner yoga, postnatal training. One generic classes page ranks for none of those terms. Specific pages match specific searches, and Google rewards the match.

faqs.q: My schedule lives inside an app. Is that a problem?
faqs.a: For SEO, yes. Google cannot read schedules trapped in apps or PDFs, and neither can a prospective member browsing at midnight. Publish the schedule as real text on a real page. Beginners boxing Tuesday 7pm is a search query; a PDF is a dead end.

faqs.q: Do reviews really matter that much for fitness?
faqs.a: More than almost anywhere. Choosing a gym or trainer is emotional, and reviews that mention instructors by name or specific results do the persuading your website cannot. A steady flow of detailed, recent reviews lifts both your map rankings and your trial bookings.

faqs.q: I'm a solo trainer, not a big gym. Can SEO work for me?
faqs.a: Often better. Individual trainers rarely invest in SEO, so a focused site with goal-specific pages and real proof can own a city's trainer searches surprisingly fast. Big-box gyms dominate ads, but they cannot out-local you.

faqs.q: What does working with you actually involve?
faqs.a: A full audit in week one, then fixes in priority order: profile, pages, reviews, booking path. Plain-English reporting throughout. You approve everything; I do the work.
